title: Same task. Different drafts.
intro: You are holding auditions. Give the products the same small job, then decide which draft earns a place in your life.
taskLabel: What would you like help with?
taskHelp: Choose something small that you can judge: an invitation, a short explanation or a plan for an ordinary day. Use your own non-sensitive material or invented details. Work information needs permission for that tool.
examplePrompt: Write a casual message to friends asking them to choose between Friday evening and Sunday afternoon for a get-together. Ask everyone to reply by Wednesday. Keep it under 60 words. Do not choose a venue or add plans I haven't supplied.
exampleHelp: This is an invented situation. Copy it as written for the comparison, or replace it with your own permitted task before trying each product.
steps: Keep the request the same in each product you try. That makes the differences easier to notice.
Paste the drafts you want to compare below. If you only have one product available, use that one; you can add the others later.
Choose what is useful, make your edits and save the version you would actually use.
exampleChecks: For the sample invitation, check the two options, the reply deadline and whether it invented a venue. Then read it aloud: does this sound like a message you would send?
finalHelp: Keep the parts that work and edit the rest. This is the version you can return to in your binder.
reflectionLabel: What would you tell a friend about using this tool for this task?
reflectionHelp: A specific observation is more useful than a permanent winner: it kept the details, needed less editing, or sounded nothing like me.
saveScope: Save your request, pasted drafts, comparisons and edits privately to your episode binder in My Closet. You can reopen, edit or delete them later.
workAdaptation: The same comparison can help with a work draft if your employer allows the tool and the information. If it doesn't, the personal task is still a complete first win.
